note: WIN-299 (M2.6). Disposition register for docs/audits/sbom/advisory/osv-report.json. scripts/audit-advisory.mjs --check fails unless EVERY CRITICAL/HIGH finding in the receipt appears here with an owner, a written argument and an unexpired review date. Entries are added BY HAND: there is deliberately no generator in the repository, because a regenerate button would mass-absolve new advisories and that is the precise failure this gate exists to prevent. scripts/verify-advisory-nonvacuity.mjs proves all seven failure modes actually fail.
policy: Two states, and they must never be confused. "waived" means somebody assessed reachability and wrote the argument down. "carried" means nobody has assessed it yet — it is an admission of unassessed risk, NOT a safety claim, and it is recorded so a live CRITICAL/HIGH cannot sit unowned the way GHSA-gr94-w7qr-f4j3 and GHSA-xwg4-73v4-xw9w did. An UPGRADED advisory is not a disposition: it stops appearing in the receipt, and is recorded under resolved[] where the gate verifies the finding is genuinely absent.
acceptance: The owner named on each entry accepts the recorded state by merging the pull request that introduces or re-dates it. A disposition authored but never merged is not an acceptance.

Present but inert: this engine.io copy is reached only through socket.io@4.7.4, whose sole parent is @trigger.dev/core@4.5.4. That package DECLARES socket.io 4.7.4 but never imports it — an exhaustive scan of the published tarball finds "socket.io-client" as the only quoted socket.io specifier (6 occurrences) and zero require("socket.io") / from "socket.io" / import("socket.io") in any build output. The engine.io server class behind this copy is therefore never constructed, and both advisories require a running Engine.IO server instance. The gateway that actually serves traffic (apps/agent + @nestjs/platform-socket.io) resolves socket.io@4.8.3 -> engine.io@6.6.9, which is patched for both. socket.io@4.7.4 pins "engine.io": "~6.5.2", so no fixed 6.5.x exists and forcing 6.6.x under it would be a combination the vendor never tested. Second, independent barrier: the vulnerable code is BaseServer.onWebTransportSession(), which has zero callers inside engine.io, is never referenced by socket.io 4.7.4 or 4.8.3, is never called by first-party code, and needs a WebTransport session object — no webtransport/http3/quic package exists in either image closure.
dispositions.durableFix: @trigger.dev/core >= 4.5.12 drops the socket.io dependency entirely (verified against the npm registry metadata for 4.5.0-4.5.16), which removes engine.io 6.5.4 from the agent closure outright. That bump also clears GHSA-p28v-f755-9qrg on @trigger.dev/core itself. It is deliberately NOT taken here: Trigger moved its realtime transport between 4.5.11 and 4.5.12, so it needs durable-execution integration validation of its own rather than riding along in a security patch.
